title: Internal Hom of Weil complexes
statement:
Fix the finite-field, coefficient and scheme data of [def-wf-weil-category]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the chosen algebraic closure, a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$, and $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Write $\mathcal C_E=D^b_c(X,E)$ for that definition's raw rationalization of the completed integral pro-etale coefficient category, $P=\Phi_X^*$ for geometric-Frobenius pullback, and $H=R\mathcal Hom_E$ for [def-wf-internal-hom].

For every two Weil pairs $(K,\varphi_K),(L,\varphi_L)$, the underlying object $H(K,L)$ belongs to $\mathcal C_E$, and the specified conjugation
$$\beta_{K,L}=H(\varphi_K^{-1},\varphi_L)\circ\alpha_{K,L}:PH(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(K,L)$$
is an isomorphism. On a pair of commuting Weil morphisms $u:K'\to K$, $v:L\to L'$, the underlying map is $H(u,v)$. These data define a bifunctor
$$H:\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,E)^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,E)\longrightarrow\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,E).$$

Its separate-variable exactness has the following precise meaning for these categories of fixed pairs. Equip a shifted pair with the datum $P(K[r])\cong(PK)[r]\xrightarrow{\varphi_K[r]}K[r]$. Consider diagrams of Weil morphisms $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ whose underlying triangle is distinguished in $\mathcal C_E$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]. With the canonical derived-Hom shift identifications, $H(K,-)$ sends every such diagram to one of the same kind, and $H(-,L)$ sends it contravariantly to
$$H(C,L)\longrightarrow H(B,L)\longrightarrow H(A,L)\longrightarrow H(C,L)[1]$$
of the same kind. In particular $H(K[r],L[s])\cong H(K,L)[s - r]$ is an isomorphism of Weil pairs, and the functor is additive and $E$-linear in each variable. This specifies preservation of underlying distinguished triangles; it does not equip the fixed-pair category with Verdier axioms.

proof.text: Use the completed ring $B=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_X$ of [def-wf-internal-hom]. The coefficient ring in [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom] is this same inverse limit, not the discrete constant sheaf. The finite-type geometry lemma [lem-cbc-compactification-geometry-fibre-bound], applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes $X$ Noetherian and finite dimensional; the field has a single Noetherian affine chart of dimension zero. It also propagates invertibility of $\ell$ from $k$ to $X$. The scheme $X$ is separated finite type over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, as required there. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], the integral category underlying [def-wf-weil-category], including its compatible etale-origin witnesses, is exactly the full completed integral category used in that corollary. Choose its integral objects $M,N$ representing $K,L$; raw rationalization changes morphisms, not objects. The corollary gives $H_B(M,N)$ in that integral category, and the characterization puts it back in the PBC category. By the definition of $H_E$ on objects in [def-wf-internal-hom], this is the required closure $H_E(K,L)\in\mathcal C_E$. No Frobenius-stable integral lattice is required.

proof.text: The ambient ringed-site functor $H_B$ carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles in both variables, reversing the first, and has the normalized shift comparisons, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. The characterization [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] makes our common full integral subcategory closed under shifts and cones. Together with Step 1, this restricts the ambient separate-variable exactness to it. Its $\mathcal O_E$-linear triangulated structure and linear shifts are those of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], applied to that common integral category. By [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated], every distinguished rational triangle is isomorphic to the image of an integral distinguished triangle. For fixed integral $M$ or $N$, apply $H_B(M,-)$ or $H_B(-,N)$ to such a triangle and then localize. The fraction rule $H_E(a/\varpi^r,b/\varpi^s)=H_B(a,b)/\varpi^{r+s}$ of [def-wf-internal-hom] identifies the result with $H_E$ of the rational triangle; isomorphic triangles have isomorphic images by functoriality. Thus $H_E$ is separately exact on $\mathcal C_E$. The same fraction rule gives additivity and $E$-linearity in each variable.

proof.text: Put $P=\Phi_X^*$. The comparison $\alpha_{K,L}:PH(K,L)\cong H(PK,PL)$ is the specified ringed-equivalence comparison in [def-wf-internal-hom]. Consequently $\beta_{K,L}=H(\varphi_K^{-1},\varphi_L)\alpha_{K,L}$ is invertible: its inverse is $\alpha_{K,L}^{-1}H(\varphi_K,\varphi_L^{-1})$, as follows by composing the two formulas and applying the bifunctor laws. Step 1 supplies its object in $\mathcal C_E$, so it is a Weil pair by [def-wf-weil-category]. A Weil pair requires one isomorphism, with no separate continuity or finite-order condition. If its positive iterates are written $\beta^{(n)}=\beta\,P\beta\cdots P^{n-1}\beta$, then $\beta^{(m+n)}=\beta^{(m)}P^m(\beta^{(n)})$ simply groups the factors; inverse factors define negative iterates. Thus the cyclic-action cocycle mentioned in the blueprint requires no use of the tensor lemma.

proof.text: Define the map of pairs by the underlying $H(u,v)$, which is admissible by Step 4. For $u':K''\to K'$ and $v':L'\to L''$, the ambient bifunctor laws in [def-wf-internal-hom] give $H(u',v')\circ H(u,v)=H(u\circ u',v'\circ v)$ and $H(1_K,1_L)=1_{H(K,L)}$. Morphisms of [def-wf-weil-category] are the underlying commuting morphisms, so these equalities also hold in the fixed-pair category. This proves the bifunctor assertion, including its variance. Addition and scalar multiplication preserve the commuting equation, and Step 2's linearity therefore holds on its Weil Hom groups.

source.place: Entire proof; completed-coefficient construction and separate-variable exactness expanded

proof.text: The normalized isomorphisms $H(K[r],L[s])\cong H(K,L)[s - r]$ are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. They intertwine the specified $\alpha$ with transport: on the Hom complex in [def-wf-internal-hom], transport acts on every local map and preserves its degree; reindexing the source or target and multiplying by the integer signs in the Hom differential commute with that transport. Exact transport preserves K-injective complexes by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport], so this calculation computes the derived comparison as well. It also commutes with the precomposition by $\varphi_K^{-1}$ and postcomposition by $\varphi_L$, by naturality of the shift identifications. Rationalization preserves these equations. Hence these are isomorphisms of Weil pairs with the shifted datum specified in the statement. Now take an equivariant triangle diagram with underlying distinguished triangle. Every output arrow, including the connecting arrow after the shift identification, is a Weil morphism by Step 4 and this shift calculation. Step 2 says the underlying output triangle is distinguished, with the usual contravariant order in the first variable. This is precisely the asserted separate-variable exactness for fixed pairs.

The characterization identifies the PBC integral category with def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed. cor-coef-integral-internal-hom gives Hom closure for all integral constructible inputs (no site-perfect hypothesis). Advisory: the Ô_{E,X} vs A_T sheaf identification rests on the characterization's stipulated-identical-coefficient clause, a DAG-wide convention. Step 2: ringed-site exactness plus closure under shifts and cones, then the scalar-localization triangle description and the fraction rule. Step 3: I verified the inverse of beta. Dropping lem-wf-tensor-weil is justified because a Weil pair needs one isomorphism and no cocycle. Step 4: I re-derived H(u,v)β = β' P(H(u,v)) with all types. Step 5: bifunctor laws. Step 6: shifts and connecting maps via presentation-transport K-injectivity. Tests: scalar point case gives mu/lambda; zero object, empty scheme, shifts of both signs. The six tool_uses are accepted as generic black boxes. prop-weil-operations is a different framework (ctf, site-perfect first argument), not a duplicate.
